messages:
rachel: quick note from a new hire onboarding session — our Go quickstart sample that does `gen.Stream(ctx, ...)` in an http.Handler hung under token-rotation stress. stack shows handshake waiting on auth refresh while handler goroutine blocks on writes. saw this on macOS and ubuntu CI.

rachel: repro sketch: start sample, hit /stream with wrk -c12 -d15s, run auth proxy that expires tokens every 2s. sporadic hangs (~3-7% runs).

tom: can you paste the handler? common pitfall is using r.Context() for both handshake and streaming.

rachel: minimal handler:```go
func StreamHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
  gen := client.Generator("lite")
  stream, err := gen.Stream(r.Context(), prompt)
  if err != nil { http.Error(w, err.Error(), 500); return }
  defer stream.Close()
  for c := range stream.Chunks() { fmt.Fprint(w, c.Text) }
}
```

aditya: yup. two UX issues hit here: (1) handshake does blocking network I/O and uses the provided ctx, (2) Close waits for internal goroutines including the handshake to finish, which means request cancellations can deadlock. New devs expect `defer stream.Close()` to always free resources.

aditya: short-term patch: perform handshake on a background ctx with a timeout, e.g.:```go
hsCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 1200*time.Millisecond)
stream, err := gen.Stream(hsCtx, prompt)
if err != nil { /* handle */ }
// then use r.Context() for reading chunks
```
This reduces hangs but isn't bulletproof if a refresh fails later.

tom: suggestion for SDK ergonomics: expose an explicit Start/Receiver API. Start(handshakeCtx, opts...) returns a lightweight Receiver immediately (handshake done async). Receiver has Chunks() and Close(). If handshake fails, Receiver emits an error token and Close still works. That way HTTP handlers can create the Receiver quickly without blocking on auth.

aditya: alternative: keep Stream(ctx) but make handshake cancel-safe and make Close preemptive (force-cancel handshake). Also add an observable `Ready() <-chan struct{}` on streams to let handlers wait for successful handshake only if they want to.

rachel: both sound reasonable. for onboarding docs we should add a "Streams in HTTP handlers" recipe explaining: 1) do a short handshake timeout on background ctx, 2) stream with request ctx, 3) always force-close on disconnect. provide sample snippet.

sdk-bot: created issue #5121: go-sdk: generator Stream ergonomics (handshake ctx, Ready(), preemptive Close). added labels devex, regression, p2 and linked repro.

tom: I'll draft a tiny API PR proposing: `type Receiver interface { Chunks() <-chan Chunk; Close() error; Ready() <-chan error }` and `StartStream(handshakeCtx context.Context, opts...) (Receiver, error)`. Ready() returns nil on success or non-nil error if handshake fails. Keep Stream(ctx) as sugar for simple scripts but deprecate if we need stronger guarantees.

aditya: please include a short migration guide and add a CI scenario that rotates tokens under load to catch regressions.

rachel: thanks — I'll attach the wrk script & auth-proxy to #5121 and paste OS/go/sdk: macOS 13.4, ubuntu-latest CI, go1.21, sdk v0.10.4. if others hit quirks, drop minimal repro here.
